properties.description: Increment 7 of epoch:planned-cognition-plus-memory, added 2026-10-29 at Anthony's word that the earlier tool-usage work is "augmented by the work here in recall/cues". It carries two decisions already accepted, now with the evidence they lacked: the process-step decision (83d2b0775fe79af6:dec:idea-process-steps-are-not-stand-alone-tools, "d then b": measure which functions are process steps from the call log, then list the step-only ones under their process tool) and the pruning decision (reflow2:dec:idea-prune-the-tool-surface-to-an-orthogonal-essential-set), under the standing rule that no tool is deleted without usage evidence and a refusing stub first. What recall and cues add: the cue counts from increments 2 and 3 tell a tool nobody wants (cued, never followed) from a tool nobody can find (never cued, never called), which is exactly what BL-155 says reflow2 cannot tell today; and a process tool listing its next step IS a cue, so grouping the six measured step pairs (mint_seat→claim_region, consumes↔provides, set_artifact_checksums→add_change_event, satisfies→add_capability, set_capability_status↔replace_text, move_component) both shrinks the surface and becomes the cue for the next call. Forced after increment 2 (it needs the counts); preferred after 3 (before/after numbers in hand) and before 6 (the named cue message is easier to define on the grouped surface). Not in it: deleting any tool without a refusing-stub release first; removing anything an MCP user relies on without a deprecating release.
properties.name: PLANNED (7, between 3 and 6) — the tool surface refined from the counts: process steps listed under their process tool, and tools pruned only on usage and cue evidence
